item.title: Stark Medical Scanner... sort of
item.description:
Let’s get this out of the way — what is “gravy blood”, and who is “Damp”?

This whole project started as an inside joke. My buddy and I would say we had gravy blood whenever we overindulged in a meal. That sluggish, heavy feeling afterward? In our lore, that’s the gravy blood kicking in.

Then one night we were watching Iron Man 2 and saw the Stark Medical Scanner. Perfect, we joked that we needed our own version to check our gravy blood levels.

item.title: Realtime BART Arrival Display
item.description: I have a love-hate relationship with BART. I’m grateful for it, but let’s just say it’s not always the most reliable so it’s nice to see before hand when the train you need is due to arrive. There are plenty of projects out there that show real-time BART arrival information. This one does that too, it’s nothing groundbreaking, but I wanted to build my own version that captures the vintage BART platform sign vibe I associate with commuting between the East Bay and my job in the city.

item.title: Nearby Aircraft Display
item.description: I have an ADS-B node feeding data into the vast network of flight trackers, but it mostly just sits on my roof humming along without any interaction from me. I can, and have, looked at the webpage that shows my local flight data and the planes on a map, but it didn’t quite have the whimsy I was after. I decided a wall-mounted device that displayed the aircraft type closest to my location at any given moment would be a fun build.
